summary.headline: Tega Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR17.2bn with 15% adjusted EBITDA margin, including one month of Molycop; consumables grew 36% YoY.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first quarter consolidating Molycop, but only for June 2026 after the June 1 closing. Consolidated revenue was about INR17.2bn and adjusted EBITDA about INR2.6bn (15% margin) before INR1.9bn of one-time acquisition and integration costs. Legacy Tega consumables delivered strong growth and margin expansion, while the equipment business fell sharply on delayed customer clearances. Management stressed that one month of Molycop is too short to draw full-year conclusions, but said June was directionally ahead of acquisition expectations.

financial_highlights.change: Prior-year one-time costs about INR0.75-0.8bn per analyst reconciliation
Income +23% YoY from INR3.72bn; EBITDA from INR0.71bn (~19%)
+3% YoY for June; described as ~30% margin in Q&A, CFO said margin flat
Down INR32.18bn (USD340mn) QoQ from INR95.8bn at March 31

segments.name: Tega Consumables
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.96bn (+36% YoY); EBITDA before one-time INR1bn at 24.1% margin (+320bps). About 23% of group revenue. Part of Q4 orders were serviced in Q1, so growth is not a clean run-rate.

segments.name: Tega Equipment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR358mn vs INR643mn (-44% YoY) due to delayed customer clearances; EBITDA roughly breakeven on lower volumes and operating leverage. About 2% of group revenue.

segments.name: Molycop (one month, June 2026)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.9bn and adjusted EBITDA INR1.6bn (~13% margin, USD17.2mn); gross margin ~36%. Volume FY (12m to Jun-26) 1.204mt vs 1.223mt prior; 12m EBITDA USD191mn, up 11% from USD172mn.

guidance_outlook: Consumables long-term revenue CAGR guidance of about 15% maintained; management called it sustainable.
Consumables EBITDA margin of 20-23% annually cited in Q&A; management said freight and commodity cost pass-through has about a one-quarter lag.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to stay around 15% for the full year.
Molycop: 10-month period volume expected up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on comparable basis; margin expected broadly flat quarter to quarter.
Molycop: about USD20mn of synergies targeted over the next two to two and a half years (SG&A, operations, procurement, scale).
Cross-selling revenue ramp expected from Q3 to Q4 FY27; quantified guidance deferred by a couple of quarters.
FY27 finance cost about INR110-120bn... stated as INR110-120 crore for the full year; Molycop 10-month interest and principal about USD70mn.
Tega capex (excluding Molycop) about USD40mn for FY27 including Chile; Molycop 10-month capex about USD28mn, normalised about low USD30mn annually.
Molycop net debt expected to decline by year-end; group divestment of non-core land parcels to repay debt, with no material EBITDA impact.
capex_capacity: Chile plant: soft commissioning around January 2027 and commercial production around March 2027, subject to local regulatory approvals expected within a two-month window.
Tega capex excluding Molycop about USD40mn for FY27 including Chile.
Molycop 10-month capex about USD28mn; normalised annual capex in low USD30mn range, with expansion-related opportunities possibly lifting it to low-to-mid USD30mn over two years.
Molycop volumes: 1.204mt in 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year.
Freeport Indonesia Grasberg: blocks 2 and 3 at planned rates; full return to planned capacity targeted by end-CY2027. Cobra Panama restart discussions ongoing.
demand_pricing: Molycop: around 85% of contracts have steel-index-linked pricing, so revenue per ton moves with steel; management tracks per-ton margin rather than percentage margin.
Molycop states above 50% market share in core regions; largest volumes in South America, with North America, Australasia and growing Africa.
Copper above USD14,000/t and gold around USD4,400/oz cited as supportive of mining investment.
Management says it has faced Chinese competition in Latin America for decades and maintains leading position via lead times, local footprint and technical support.

Freight costs have risen; Tega passes through freight in contracts with a quarter lag; Molycop hedges ocean freight and passes through land costs linked to gas prices. No material deferment of shipments seen.
Equipment shortfall attributed to customer clearance delays rather than demand loss.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue ramp from cross-selling across Tega and Molycop networks, beyond the USD20mn cost synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the revenue ramp is expected from Q3 to Q4 FY27; it is early days, and quantified guidance will come in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Molycop's margin seasonal, is the current margin steady state, and are there one-off RM or macro items?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said there is little quarter-to-quarter seasonality, June was historically Molycop's strongest quarter, and margin should be relatively flat in coming quarters. Molycop manages to per-ton margin because about 85% of contracts are steel-index linked.

qa_highlights.question: Chile plant commissioning status?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka said the plant is on track for soft commissioning around January 2027 and commercial production around March 2027, subject to local regulatory clearances expected within a two-month window.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any further one-time costs beyond the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mohanka confirmed the Q1 one-time costs are the full amount. The analyst tallied INR110cr this year plus about INR75-80cr last year, totalling about INR190cr, which management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Group and Molycop debt levels and year-end expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi said group total debt is INR112bn including about INR26bn of redeemable preference shares. Patrick Koley said Molycop net debt was USD672mn at June 30 and is expected to fall by year-end, with ABL swings driven by bar payments.

qa_highlights.question: Molycop capex and volume outlook, plus Latin America competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Patrick Koley said 10-month capex is about USD28mn, normalised capex is in the low USD30mn range, and volume is expected up about 5% and EBITDA up about 4% on a 10-month comparable basis. Volume was 1.204mt for the 12 months to June 2026 vs 1.223mt prior year. Lance Dawber said Molycop has competed with China for decades and retains its lead through lead times and local support.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 finance cost, Tega capex, and consumables growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Ravi Joshi guided FY27 finance cost to INR110-120cr and Tega capex excluding Molycop to about USD40mn including Chile. Mehul Mohanka maintained about 15% consumables CAGR and said pass-through of costs has a one-quarter lag, supporting a 20-23% margin.

risks_watch: Integration and synergy delivery: about USD20mn targeted over 2-2.5 years; cross-sell revenue quantification deferred by a couple of quarters.
Only one month of Molycop (June 2026) is consolidated; the 10-month outlook (volume +5%, EBITDA +4%) is not yet a full run-rate read. Watch the Q2 print.
Equipment revenue fell 44% YoY on customer clearance delays; order book executable within one year is stated as INR9.6 million in the transcript, likely a typo for INR9.6bn, and needs confirmation.
Chile plant timing depends on local regulatory approvals; any slip beyond March 2027 would delay commercial production.
Freight and container availability: pass-through has about a one-quarter lag, and Molycop's land freight is linked to gas prices. Molycop's per-ton margin is exposed to steel index movements.

Deleveraging depends on non-core land divestments (no amount or timing given) and on Molycop working-capital swings from bar payments; FX exposure is partly hedged, with Spain and Australia operations outside USD.
Molycop margin figures are inconsistent in the call: about 13% (INR1.6bn on INR12.9bn) versus about 30% cited in a Q&A question, which management did not clearly reconcile.
key_quotes: Before moving to the quarterly performance update, I would like to emphasize that this is the first quarter in which Molycop's performance for the month of June 2026 has been consolidated into Tega's financial result of Q1 FY27.
It would be premature to draw conclusions regarding the full year outlook based on this number of Molycop.
So, request a couple of quarters of patience with us and we'll be able to give you a more definitive number around it.
We're maintaining our guidance of about 15% CAGR on the consumables.
We haven't seen much of deferment, but yes, that does, you know, contribute in terms of logistic challenges in terms of container availability, frequency of mother vessels coming to port.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the legacy Tega consumables business and on Molycop's June momentum, but cautious on forward numbers, since management repeatedly said one month of Molycop is too short to draw full-year conclusions. It was more evasive on cross-sell revenue and Chile timing, deferring quantified guidance and stressing that approvals are "anyone's guess".

growth.why: Consumables grew 36% YoY and consumables CAGR of about 15% was held, with Molycop consolidated for one month and Chile plant commercial production targeted March 2027; offset by equipment revenue down 44% YoY and Molycop volumes down slightly over 12 months (1.204mt vs 1.223mt).
